key: Therefore the sage puts his own person last, and yet it is found in the foremost place; he treats his person as if it were foreign to him, and yet that person is preserved.
s: The chapter says the sage puts his person last and it is found foremost, treats it as foreign and it is preserved; the Heshang Gong commentary, on chapter 7, reads this as putting others first, taking little for himself and giving much to others, so that the world honours him and the people love him as father and mother.
src: The Heshang Gong commentary, Laozi Daodejing Heshang Gong zhangju, chapter 7, zh.wikisource (a normalised text), revision 2019760 (2021)

evidence.words: 先人而後己也。…天下敬之，先以為長。…薄己而厚人也。…百姓愛之如父母，神明祐之若赤子，故身常存。
evidence.gloss: (On putting his person last:) he puts others first and himself after. (On its being foremost:) all under heaven revere him and put him first as their elder. (On treating his person as foreign:) he is sparing to himself and generous to others. (On its being preserved:) the people love him as father and mother, the spirits protect him as an infant, so his person always endures.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref Tao Te Ching 7, at [6]). The Heshang Gong base text 是以聖人後其身，而身先，外其身，而身存 is the line of the key verse, and its comment on each clause carries every element of the reading: others first and self after, sparing to self and generous to others, revered by all under heaven, loved by the people as father and mother. Plain sense restates the key verse without Legge's additions. entry-check ok.
